FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.

2. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.

3. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. fenêtre
   B. porte
   C. livre
   D. chaise

4. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good morning / hello
   B. Thank you
   C. Good night only
   D. Excuse me

5. When practising Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

7. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

8. When practising Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

9. When practising Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.

10. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Oral expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
